title: Sustainable Food Value Chains for Nutrition
provider: FAO elearning Academy (Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations)
language: English, Spanish, French (course-specific). The FAO elearning Academy platform overall hosts courses in 9 languages including Russian, but THIS course is offered in EN/ES/FR only — no Russian version verified.
cost: Free (no fee). Registration/account on elearning.fao.org required.
certificate: Digital badge (Open Badge model used across the FAO Academy) issued upon completing the course AND passing the final certification exam with a minimum grade of 75%.
duration: ~2 hours 30 minutes total; individual lessons range ~20-55 minutes each.
level: Intermediate — aimed at practitioners (level not formally labelled on the page; inferred from target audience as intermediate). [UNVERIFIED as an explicit page label]
target_audience: Development practitioners, policy makers, extension agents, researchers, and private-sector professionals working on sustainable food systems and nutrition-sensitive value chains.
format: Self-paced online e-learning (browser-based: Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox); also downloadable as a standalone package (Windows PC only, ~24MB). Moodle-based LMS, mobile-friendly platform.
assessment: Single final certification exam; pass threshold 75%. Badge awarded on pass.
hands_on: Applied activities embedded in lessons — commodity/value-chain analysis and SFVCN project-design exercises (walking learners through framing, impact pathways, and designing a project). No external software/data lab; activities are in-course interactive exercises. [Hands-on depth UNVERIFIED beyond page summary]
tools: No external/specialized software required — fully in-browser self-contained course. Conceptual frameworks used: FAO Sustainable Food Value Chain (SFVC) framework and SFVCN impact-pathway model.

syllabus.module: Lesson 1 — Introduction to nutrition and sustainable food value chains
syllabus.topics: Core concepts linking nutrition and value chains; rationale for an SFVCN approach; key terminology and the malnutrition/food-system problem framing.

syllabus.module: Lesson 2 — Framing sustainability and nutrition in value chains
syllabus.topics: How sustainability (economic, social, environmental) and nutrition outcomes are integrated into the FAO SFVC framework; positioning nutrition within value-chain analysis.

syllabus.module: Lesson 3 — Supporting nutritional outcomes through SFVCN impact pathways
syllabus.topics: Impact-pathway logic; how interventions along the value chain translate into improved nutrition outcomes; supply- and demand-side levers.
Applying the framework to design a nutrition-sensitive value-chain project; commodity selection/analysis, intervention design, and project-design activity.

strengths: Genuinely $0-cost with a recognized, verifiable digital badge (Open Badge) gated behind a 75% exam — credible credential at zero price.
Tight, completable scope: 4 lessons / ~2.5 hours total lowers drop-off for busy practitioners.
Clear pedagogical arc: concept -> framing -> impact pathways -> hands-on project design (theory ends in an applied design task).
Practitioner-oriented audience framing (extension agents, private sector, policy) closely matches an SMB agro audience.
Multilingual delivery (EN/ES/FR for this course; platform supports 9 languages incl. Russian) — proven model for localization.
Offline/downloadable package option supports low-connectivity learners.
Backed by an authoritative institution (FAO) with a published SFVC framework underpinning the content.
weaknesses: No Russian version of THIS course — directly limits reuse for a Russian-language North-Kazakhstan audience.
Short and high-level: 2.5h cannot deliver deep technical/operational skill; it is awareness/framework-level, not a how-to for field practice.
Single end-of-course exam (no per-lesson formative quizzes confirmed) is a thin assessment design.
Downloadable package is Windows-only — excludes other devices for offline use.
No region-specific cases (nothing for Central Asia / dryland cereal-livestock systems); generic global examples.
No live/cohort or mentoring component — fully self-paced, which can lower completion for less-motivated SMB learners.
Hands-on is in-course exercises only — no real datasets, tools, or transferable artifacts the learner keeps.
borrow_for_folur: Adopt the badge-gated-by-exam model: issue a free verifiable credential (Open Badge spec) only after a >=75% final test — credible and $0, fits the platform's GitHub Pages + cert-engine stack.

Copy the 4-step learning arc (concept -> framing -> impact pathway -> applied project design) as a reusable module template, ending every module in an applied design/analysis task rather than a passive read.
Keep modules short and completable (~2-2.5h, ~4 lessons) to reduce drop-off among busy SMB agro practitioners — mirror this length cap per FOLUR module.

Make the value-chain framework explicit and reusable (FAO SFVC framework + impact-pathway diagram) — adapt it to North-Kazakhstan cereal/livestock/FOLUR commodity chains with regional cases (СКО/Костанай/Акмола) to fix FAO's gap of generic examples.
Provide a downloadable/offline package per module for low-connectivity rural learners — but make it cross-platform (not Windows-only) to beat FAO's limitation.
Treat the multilingual delivery as the headline differentiator: deliver FOLUR content fully in Russian (Cyrillic) since FAO leaves this course EN/ES/FR-only — a clear localization gap to own.

Improve on FAO's thin assessment: add short per-lesson formative quizzes (использовать движок test_engine с генерацией вариантов) plus the gating final exam, so learners self-check before the 75% gate.
